topics.topic: Failure details returned by discard_new_store and required start diagnostic wording
questions: What failure information does this operation provide to `instance_lifecycle`, and exactly what must the start diagnostic say, given that the declared output is only a boolean and the operation declares no error?
When closing the connection fails, must that close failure be named in the start diagnostic, be described as a failed removal, or remain unreported?

When closing the store connection fails before any removal is attempted, must the start diagnostic also say that the store was left, must it name a close failure, or must it mention only the listener failure?

How does discard_new_store tell instance_lifecycle whether the failure was the connection close or which companion/store removal failed, when its only declared output is the boolean saying whether the main store file is gone?

quotes:
Whether it was removed: true when the store's file is gone; false
otherwise.

The first close or removal that fails stops the rest, so the
store's file is removed only after its companions are: what a failure
leaves is the store's file with some of its companions, an empty store of
the release's version, which the next start opens as any store.

None; a failed removal is named in the start's one diagnostic beside the
surface that could not be opened.

One that cannot be opened stops
the start with a diagnostic naming the surface: the listeners already
opened are closed, then a store step 3 made new is removed, then the
process ends with its one diagnostic, which names the surface that could
not be opened and, when the new store could not be removed, that it was
left; a close that fails is not named — the process's end releases the
listener — and a store step 3 made new is removed by
`capability:store.discard_new_store` — one it cannot remove is an empty
store of the release's version, which the next start opens as any store
(A17 rule 2).
judgement.divergence: After a companion removal or the store-connection close fails, one implementation communicates only false and the diagnostic generically says the new store was left; another communicates the failed close or pathname and the diagnostic names that specific cleanup failure. The host owner sees the difference.
judgement.why: The operation promises that a failed removal is named but exposes only a gone/not-gone boolean and does not specify whether or how a close failure or particular failed pathname is communicated.

witness.initial: A listener cannot be opened after a new store and regular `-wal` and `-shm` companions exist, and removal of `-shm` is denied.
events: Removal of `-shm` fails and stops cleanup.
The start emits its one diagnostic.
outcomes: The boolean false leads to a generic diagnostic saying that the new store was left.
Unspecified failure details identify that removal of `-shm` failed beside the failed listener surface.
witness.observer: The host owner reading the start diagnostic.
basis:
Nothing is served until every check passed; a listener that cannot be
opened closes the one already opened and has `store.discard_new_store`
remove a store this start made new (A17 rule 2); a restart ends every owner
session (A13 rule 2). It decides no check.

The store's one connection — `open_store` opens no other — is closed; then,
in this order, the companion files SQLite may keep beside the store under
its name with a suffix, `-wal`, `-shm`, `-journal`, each removed when it is
a regular file, and last the store's file. A path of another type is left
as it is. The first close or removal that fails stops the rest, so the
store's file is removed only after its companions are: what a failure
leaves is the store's file with some of its companions, an empty store of
the release's version, which the next start opens as any store.

topics.topic: Whether regular-file classification follows symbolic links
questions: Is a symbolic link to a regular file a regular file for this rule, or a path of another type that must be left untouched?
Is a symbolic link to a regular file considered a regular file here, or must the test examine the directory entry without following links?

Is a companion path that is a symbolic link to a regular file considered a regular file and removed, or considered a path of another type and left? The text must specify whether the type test follows symbolic links.

quotes:
The store's one connection — `open_store` opens no other — is closed; then,
in this order, the companion files SQLite may keep beside the store under
its name with a suffix, `-wal`, `-shm`, `-journal`, each removed when it is
a regular file, and last the store's file. A path of another type is left
as it is.
judgement.divergence: A following regular-file test removes a companion pathname that is a symbolic link to a regular file; a non-following test classifies the symbolic-link entry as another type and leaves it. The host owner inspecting the directory notices.
judgement.why: The text requires a regular-file classification but does not say whether that classification follows symbolic links.

witness.initial: A new store exists and its `-wal` pathname is a symbolic link to a regular file.
outcomes: A following type test classifies the target as regular and removes the symbolic-link entry.
A non-following type test classifies the directory entry as a symbolic link and leaves it.
witness.observer: The host owner inspecting the store directory.

topics.topic: Cleanup continuation policy and exact files permitted to remain after removal failures
questions: Must cleanup stop at the first failure, or must it continue trying every removable file so that A17's guarantee that a failed start leaves no file it made except one it could not remove remains true?
What must remain when all companion removals succeed but removal of the store file itself fails?

Exactly which files may remain after each possible failure? A failure removing the store file occurs after every removable companion is gone, so it can leave the store file with no companion, while an early failure can leave all companions, contrary to the single description "with some of its companions".
Does the permitted "empty store made new" residue include every SQLite companion left after discard_new_store stops, or must the failed start leave only the main store file?

the release's version, which the next start opens as any store.

   run removes with the other temporary files (A18 rule 4); a file of the

   store it made new for a start a listener then failed, which it removes —
   one it cannot remove is an empty store of the release's version, which the
   next start opens as any store.
